# Review — cid-tiradas-64-68 (tiradas 64–68, lines 1085–1155)

Adversarial review against the pinned packet, Pidal's rubrics and footnotes on the scan (PDF pp. 203–207 read at
150 dpi, with a crop at 400 dpi of vv. 1110–1116 to settle sí at v. 1115), conventions.md, the pilot (01-04) and
the published parts (especially 18-18, 32-34, 49-55, 56-59 and 60-63), the shared glossary and known-forms.json.
All edits made by script (json load/dump, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1). No `t` changed: the 71 `t` lines
concatenated equal the packet's 71 lines exactly (checked by script before and after the edits); one `l` line per
`t` line in all 29 units.

Checked and found sound (no change):
- Cantar heading on PDF p. 203 (CANTAR SEGUNDO · BODAS DE LAS HIJAS DEL CID) reported right.
- Rubrics against the scan: 64 El Cid se dirige contra tierras de Valencia; 65 Toma de Murviedro; 66 Los moros
  valencianos cercan al Cid. Éste reúne sus gentes.—Arenga; 67 Fin de la arenga del Cid; 68 Minaya da el plan de
  batalla. El Cid vence otra lid campal.—Toma de Cebolla. All five right. Assonances re-derived from the line ends:
  64 á; 65 é-o; 66 á (plaze, fazen, salve á-e); 67 á-a; 68 á (Fáñez, plaze, Yague, tendales, traen with unstressed
  final). Right in all five first notes; the note to 67 rightly says the Çid's speech runs on across the change of
  assonance (Pidal sets the continuation quote ” at 1122).
- Footnotes against the scan, wording right: 1087 (asentarse definitivamente en las tierras del rey de Lérida; comp.
  958, 951, págs. 15 y 16), 1090 (contra 'hacia'; Más y Prat, 1885), 1092 (now with its boundary marked), 1095
  (29 km; 1098; comp. nota anterior), 1112 (eñadir o añadir en algo, 'aumentar algo', 'aumentarán nuestro
  provecho'), 1118 (grado a Dios 'gracias a Dios', v. 792), 1124 ('atacaremos aquel su ejército', v. 1224), 1131
  (ferredes 'heriréis'; ataque combinado, p. 98), 1140 (el caudillo gritaba su nombre …, 721), 1142 (acostarse los
  tendales 'ladearse, caerse los postes …'; v. 2400), 1143, 1145 (maguer les pesa 'aunque les pesa', 3116), 1151
  (de piedes de cavallo 'a uña de caballo'), 1150 (Cebolla < jubayla 'montecito'; el Puig, 18 km; 1093), 1154
  (nuevas 'renombre, fama', 1556, 1206, 2084). The note to 1159 on p. 207 belongs to the next part. No other
  footnotes on these pages; the notes that say "Pidal gives no note" (ducá, 1102b, 1106, 1125–1126, quis, the
  reordering) are right.
- Print order and numbering against the margin of p. 207: 1145, 1151, 1147, (1148, 1149), 1152, 1153, 1146, 1150,
  1155, 1154 — exactly as the note to 1144 says; 1086 printed at the end of tirada 63 (part 60-63) and 1085 at the
  head of 64; 1102b printed in roman with its b-number. The tirada-68 notes keep Pidal's print order and numbers
  and say so; 1155 before 1154 explained by the opening of tirada 69 (Sonando van sus nuevas, v. 1156, on p. 207).
- Italics seen on the image and reported correctly: [h]a (1088, 1089), vi[d]íe, s'[a]n, f[o] (twice), se[e]d,
  ve[e]r, R[o]y, [cr]ebar, pie[de]s. sí (1115) accented, confirmed at 400 dpi; tomós (1102) so printed (not
  tornós); Myo (1092) and Álbar with accent so printed.
- Grammar labels checked and right: Aquis (= aquí se), Poblado ha / dexado [h]a (aver + participle first),
  conquistas las ha (short participle agreeing), Ayudól, priso, vi[d]íe (old imperfect), iva valiendo, sabet, quel,
  viniessen çercar (venir + bare inf.), Trasnocharon / tornan (tense-mixing), Viólo, tomós (tomarse a + inf.),
  femosles (femos = fazemos), el so pan (article + possessive), nos çercar vienen, vayan (jussive), desí, luego 'at
  once', conpeçaremos, eñadrán (syncopated future), juntados s'[a]n (participle agreeing with todos), sí + optative
  subjunctive, partiemos / pudiemos (-iemos), double negative ni … non, çercados nos han (agreeing with nos),
  quisiéremos (fut. subj.), firme mientre, son … a escarmentar, se[e]d (imperative of seer), pareçrá (syncopated
  future), dedes (polite subj.), firádeslos (subj. of ferir + los), ferredes (future), i avrá, del otra part, gelo,
  a dicho, piénssanse de, ha de far, ferirlos va, d'apostol / d'amor, so = soy, veriedes, entróles, oviéronse a,
  ques, es alcaz, segudar (infinitive as noun), fechas ha (agreeing), an = han, qué se far, sonando van.
- House renderings and consistency: "my Çid" and "Vivar" in `i`, Bivar in `l` (as 56-59, 60-63); Minaya Álvar
  Fáñez in `i`, Álbar in `l` (Pidal prints Álbar here, so the `l` keeps his accent); Roy Díaz in `l`, Ruy Díaz in
  `i`; "the spiritual Father" (house; 18-18); "Thanks be to thee" (pilot v. 8); "he who was born in a good hour";
  almofalla "host" (32-34); "Short of a battle" (56-59); "set about" for pensar de + inf.; mesnadas "companies".
- `l` ↔ `i` checked unit by unit; no remembered English found. 1106 `i` supplies the negative the sense requires;
  the note says the line has none and cites vv. 983 and 989 (verified in 56-59).
- Part name: the drafter's "Toward Valencia: Murviedro taken, the Moors of Valencia routed" accepted in place of
  parts.json's "… and the Moorish armies beaten": the besiegers are the men of Valencia (v. 1098), the rout runs to
  Valencia (v. 1148), and the name is shorter and exact. titleEn and part agree; "lines 1085–1155" gives the
  numeric range (min–max), as 60-63 did (1024–1086), though Pidal's last printed line is 1154.

Findings refused:
- 1088 ducá read as d'acá 'of this side': no footnote, the vocabulario is not in the repository and the OCR is not
  a source; the note already says the reading is uncertain. Left.
- 1136 quis 'each' (Latin quisque) strengthening cada: hedged in the note; the form is real (quis cada uno is the
  Old Spanish 'each and every one'). Left.
- 1106 partirá 'settle, decide': the note's reading and hedge are adequate; an alternative 'get us clear of it'
  (cf. quitar at v. 983) comes to the same sense. Left.
- 1087 `i` "settled in the pass": poblar is transitive ('has settled/occupied the pass'); the English is a fair
  rendering. Left.
- 1125 `i` "gone out from their own land into a strange one": interpretive, but the note gives both readings and
  the hedge. Left.
- 1150 note "(cebolla is Spanish for 'onion')" inside the paraphrase of Pidal's note: a parenthesis, plainly ours.
  Left.
- 1092 Huesa "a town of Teruel, not Huesca": already in the shared glossary from Pidal; not on these pages but sound.
  Left.

Checked: gloss keys (75, excluding __broaden__) equal the novel-forms.json keys exactly. Every __broaden__ value
(14: es, estraña, avrá, dar, de, commo, tornós, por, fincar, nuevas, so, su, piedes, veer) begins with the
cid-glossary.json entry whole, byte for byte, then " · " (checked by script; known-forms.json agrees with the
glossary for every one). All tokens of the 71 lines (brackets stripped, lowercased, apostrophe splitting) are covered
by known + gloss. Other entries checked and right in lemma and grammar: conpieça, gesta, mar, salada, guerrear,
orient, exe, xérica, onda, almenar, borriana, ayudól, murviedro, vidíe, valiendo, viniessen, trasnocharon, alva,
viólo, maravillar, femosles, bevemos, comemos, partirá (hedged), vayan, deven, ayudar, alucad, vengan,
conpeçaremos, fío, compeçó, salve, linpia, ni, pudiemos, çercados, quisiéremos, durar, escarmentar, venga,
aparejados, pareçrá, mereçe, fagamos, pido, firádeslos (pres. subj. 2nd pl. + los), quis (hedged), alvores,
ferirlos, apostol, cuerda, arrancarse, estacas, entróles, oviéronse, arrancar, ques (que + se), pudieron, fechas,
robavan, sonando; broadens es ('that', es alcaz, es logar), estraña ('foreign'), avrá (impersonal 'there will be'),
de (de + inf. after a verb), commo ('as soon as', 'since'), por (fiar por) kept, each a sense the known entry lacks.
No other broaden missing: a (a dicho = ha), an (= han), ha de far (aver de, under the de broaden), i 'there', sí
optative, a menos de (under menos), pro 'profit', luego, desí, quanto, mientre, exidos, soldada, alcaz, segudar,
campo, poblado ('settled'), contra 'toward' are covered.

Findings refused:
- sabe known as 'she knows' (subject here a man): an old entry, general enough (as tornós 'she' was left in
  60-63). Left.
- fo known entry speaks of "this part's three occurrences": an old entry pinned to its part; not ours to change
  outside a broaden. Left.
- de broaden for de + infinitive after a verb: arguably covered by the old entry's "de + infinitive after an
  adjective", but the verbal use (començar de, pensar de, aver de) is distinct and frequent. Left.
- tornan 'set to' (tornan tiendas a fincar): the known entry's tornan de castigar 'go back to' is close enough.
  Left.

## Readings left uncertain

- v. 1088 ducá: d'acá 'of this side' taken; a place or district name possible; no footnote.
- v. 1106 A menos de lid aquesto nos partirá: no negative in the line; the sense 'this will not be settled without a
  battle' is taken from context and vv. 983, 989; no footnote.
- v. 1112 eñadrán: subject unnamed (most naturally the men summoned).
- v. 1125 Commo omnes exidos de tierra estraña: loose syntax; both readings in the note.
- v. 1136 quis cada uno: quis < quisque, 'each and every'; no footnote.
- Pidal gives no reason for his reordering of vv. 1146–1155 on these pages.

## For the owner

- No defect seen in the pinned text: the italics and marks listed above agree with the scan (the text was not
  re-collated letter by letter in this review). Pidal prints an opening quote “ at the head of v. 1133 inside
  Minaya's speech (a printer's slip for the continuation mark ”); the pinned text rightly carries no quote there.
